formats.key: safeRouteSingle((uint8 tokenType,bytes data) tokenIn,(uint8 tokenType,bytes data) tokenOut,address receiver,bytes data)
effects: The router takes the input amount of the ERC-20 token in tokenIn from the signer and sends it to the EnsoShortcuts contract, which spends the signer's allowance to the router.
The hidden route data runs in the EnsoShortcuts contract and decides which swaps happen and where the tokens go.
The call reverts unless the receiver's balance of the tokenOut token grows by at least the minimum amount.
No native value can leave: tokenType must be ERC20 (mustMatch 1), and routeSingle reverts when msg.value is not 0 for a non-native input.
formats.shown: "Route 10 USDC via Enso, at least 9.95 USDT0 to <receiver>" with fields Amount (token and amount), Minimum received (token and amount) and Receiver; the token types are checked to be ERC20 and the route is hidden.

findings.title: safeRouteSingle intent says 'Route tokens' and the sentence has no verb for receiving the output token.
findings.evidence: descriptor safeRouteSingle: intent "Route tokens via Enso", interpolatedIntent "Route {#.tokenIn.data.[32:64]} via Enso, at least {#.tokenOut.data.[32:64]} to {#.receiver}"; case 0 renders "Route 10 USDC via Enso, at least 9.95 USDT0 to 0x5aAe…". EnsoRouter.safeRouteSingle is a swap with a minimum-output check (_checkMinAmountOut).
findings.fix: Set intent to "Swap tokens via Enso" and interpolatedIntent to "Swap {#.tokenIn.data.[32:64]} for at least {#.tokenOut.data.[32:64]} to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: safeRouteSingle hides the route bytes; only the minimum output to the receiver is enforced.
findings.evidence: EnsoRouter._execute: shortcuts.call{value: msg.value}(data); _checkMinAmountOut: if (amountOut < minAmountOut) revert. Descriptor field #.data 'Route' visible never.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can decode the weiroll route. A minimum of 0 removes all protection, so wallets should warn on it.

findings.title: safeRouteSingle with a native POL or NFT input or output cannot be clear signed because of mustMatch [1].
findings.evidence: EnsoRouter._transfer handles TokenType Native, ERC721, ERC1155; descriptor tokenType fields use visible {mustMatch:[1]}, and data slices [12:32]/[32:64] fit only the ERC20 layout.
findings.fix: Nothing to change now: the native layout (uint256 only) does not fit the ERC20 slices. A separate format per token type needs spec support for conditional paths.

formats.key: safeRouteMulti((uint8 tokenType,bytes data)[] tokensIn,(uint8 tokenType,bytes data)[] tokensOut,address receiver,bytes data)
effects: The router takes each ERC-20 amount listed in tokensIn from the signer and sends it to the EnsoShortcuts contract, which spends the signer's allowances to the router.
The hidden route data runs in the EnsoShortcuts contract and decides which swaps happen and where the tokens go.
For each tokensOut entry, the call reverts unless the receiver's balance of that token grows by at least its minimum. Each entry is checked separately against the same starting balance.
No native value can leave: every tokenType must be ERC20 (mustMatch 1), and routeMulti reverts when msg.value is not 0 and no native input is present.
formats.shown: "Route 9.998579 USDC.e and 0.00043 USDC via Enso, at least 9.9 USDT0 to <receiver>" with one Amount field per input token, one Minimum received per output token, and Receiver; the route is hidden.

findings.title: safeRouteMulti intent says 'Route tokens' and the sentence has no verb for receiving the output tokens.
findings.evidence: descriptor safeRouteMulti: intent "Route tokens via Enso"; case 1 renders "Route 9.998579 USDC.e and 0.00043 USDC via Enso, at least 9.9 USDT0 to 0x5aAe…".
findings.fix: Set intent to "Swap tokens via Enso" and interpolatedIntent to "Swap {#.tokensIn.[].data.[32:64]} for at least {#.tokensOut.[].data.[32:64]} to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: safeRouteMulti hides the route bytes, and an empty tokensOut array removes every output check.
findings.evidence: EnsoRouter.safeRouteMulti: for (uint256 i; i < tokensOut.length; ++i) _checkMinAmountOut(...); _execute forwards data to shortcuts. Descriptor #.data visible never.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can require a non-empty tokensOut. Wallets should warn when no 'Minimum received' field shows.

findings.title: safeRouteMulti checks a token listed twice in tokensOut against one balance increase, not their sum.
findings.evidence: EnsoRouter.safeRouteMulti records balances[i] before the route, then _checkMinAmountOut per entry: amountOut = balance - prevBalance for each entry independently.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can fix this. Two 'Minimum received' lines for the same token guarantee only the larger one.

findings.title: safeRouteMulti with native POL or NFT entries cannot be clear signed because of mustMatch [1].
findings.evidence: EnsoRouter._transfer supports Native, ERC721, ERC1155; descriptor #.tokensIn.[].tokenType and #.tokensOut.[].tokenType use visible {mustMatch:[1]}.

findings.format: safeRouteSingle((uint8 tokenType,bytes data) tokenIn,(uint8 tokenType,bytes data) tokenOut,address receiver,bytes data)
findings.title: safeRouteSingle is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: The descriptor only signs ERC20 inputs: #.tokenIn.tokenType has mustMatch [1], and the wallet raises an error on any other value. With a non-Native input, routeSingle reverts on any non-zero msg.value, so this function can never keep or forward ETH on a screen the descriptor shows.
findings.quote: EnsoRouter.routeSingle (called by safeRouteSingle): `bool isNativeAsset = _transfer(tokenIn); if (!isNativeAsset && msg.value != 0) revert WrongMsgValue(msg.value, 0);` — descriptor.json safeRouteSingle: {"path": "#.tokenIn.tokenType", "visible": {"mustMatch": [1]}}
